component.name: streamboat
component.summary: Play TIDAL with your own subscription; not affiliated with TIDAL

description.p: streamboat is an open-source client for TIDAL, for people who already pay for a TIDAL subscription. It talks to the same unofficial api.tidal.com API that other open-source TIDAL clients — High Tide and Sone — use, so it needs your own active TIDAL subscription and does not work without one. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by TIDAL in any way.

streamboat is a player, not a downloader. It never decrypts protected streams, never requests TIDAL's own licensed offline mode, never pools credentials across accounts, and never produces a playable file that outlives your subscription. An encrypted manifest is refused, loudly, with an explanation, rather than worked around.

By default, streamboat reports what you played back to TIDAL once you've listened to more than 30 seconds of it, the same way TIDAL's own apps do, so Recently Played and personalization behave the way you would expect. This is disclosed, not hidden, and can be turned off entirely in settings.

ul.li: Gapless playback, all four TIDAL quality tiers up to Hi-Res Lossless
Optional bit-perfect / exclusive-mode output (no OS resampling or mixing)
A headless daemon mode for a Raspberry Pi or a server, alongside the desktop app

screenshot.caption: streamboat's desktop shell (not built yet — see docs/architecture.md)

description.p: First playable milestone: a command-line spike. Device-code login, search, manifest resolution through the quality cascade, and gapless playback through GStreamer on Linux with a selectable ALSA output device. The desktop shell and Windows/macOS support are not in this release yet.
